name: The Children's Aid Society, Mumbai.
description: In the year 1921, the Government of Bombay expressed in the Legislative Council, its resolve to bring in a Children's Act. Three years later {1924} the Bombay Children's Act was passed. Eventually, in November, 1926, Sir Earnest Hotson, the then Home Member, Government of Bombay convened a conference of Social Workers, which led to the formation of the Children's Aid Society on March 1927. His Excellency Sir Leslie Wilson was the President and the Hon'ble Mr. E. B. Hotson C. S. I., I. C. S. was the Chairman and the Committee consisted of eminent persons of the time.

featured_reviews.name: Farzana Yasmin
featured_reviews.review_text:
Since childhood, I have been visiting Mahim Dargah with my family for ziyarat and returning thereafter. However, I have always observed certain practices taking place there that deeply concern me from an Islamic perspective.

There are women who appear to act possessed, often chained, and people are encouraged to believe in these displays. Many visitors are seen making dua to the Baba buried there, instead of making dua to Allah for him. Such acts go against the teachings of the Qur’an and the Sunnah, which clearly prohibit associating partners with Allah or seeking help from anyone other than Him.

Allah ﷻ says in the Qur’an:

> "And that the masjids are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone along with Allah."
(Surah Al-Jinn, 72:18)

And in another verse:

> "Do not call upon anyone besides Allah; such a one can neither benefit you nor harm you."
(Surah Yunus, 10:106)

Our beloved Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said:

> "When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah."
(Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516)

Recently, my mother, who is a patient and cannot sit with her legs folded, had to straighten her leg for comfort. Some individuals objected, saying that she should not keep her leg straight as the maqam (resting place) of the Baba and his companions is nearby. However, Islam teaches us only to show such respect toward the Qibla, not graves.

These practices—bowing, seeking favors, or believing others have divine power—are not part of Islam. Instead, they contradict the pure message of Tawheed (Oneness of Allah) that the Qur’an and Prophet Muhammad ﷺ emphasized.

May Allah guide us all to the right path and protect us from shirk and bid’ah (innovations in religion).
Ameen.
